newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bear Stearns sees strong Cemex performance in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns sees strong Cemex performance in 1997.

text.p: Mexico's Cemex SA should perform very well this year because of expected higher demand for cement in Mexico and Venezuela, Bear Stearns said on Tuesday.

"A strong increase in demand is expected in Mexico and Venezuela ... and even though growth could diminish in the United States, our previous expectations were too conservative," Bear Stearns analysts Sobani Warner and Daniel Altman wrote in an Latin American cement and construction outlook for 1997.

The analysts reiterated their "buy" recommendation, saying Cemex's over-the-counter shares in the United States could reach 10-1/4 by the end of 1997. The American Depositary Receipts were trading recently as 8-41/64.
In 1996, Cemex opened 1,000 new stores and distributorships in Mexico, which should allow it to compete more effectively against chief rival Apasco SA de CV, the analysts said.
The report said Cemex Mexico's sales volumes should reach 13.715 million tonnes, up eight percent from 1996, when sales volumes were little changed from the previous year.
Exports from Cemex's Mexican operation were expected to reach 4.25 million tonnes, about the same as in 1996.
The analysts said the Venezuelan government's plan to spend $1.0 billion on low-income housing during the next five or six years should benefit Vencemos SA , Cemex's Venezuelan unit.

Warner and Altman said Vencemos could provide 13.7 percent of Cemex's consolidated cash and post sales volume growth of 6.5 percent in 1997 and 12 percent in 1998. However, exports could fall by 5.6 percent and 11.7 percent in each of the next two years, they said.
